title: 反相加法器
statement: 图示反相加法器中，v_1 = 1 V，v_2 = 2 V，R_1 = 10 kΩ，R_2 = 20 kΩ，R_f = 30 kΩ，运放为理想运放。
求反馈电阻中的电流 i_f 和输出电压 v_o。

questions.ask: 若 v_2 改为 4 V，R_1 中的电流 i_1 会怎样变化？
choiceExplain: i_f 确实会变大，但多出来的电流来自哪一路？想一想 n 点的电位会不会随 v_2 改变。
v_2 增大会抬高 n 点的电位吗？想一想运放怎样调整 v_o、n 点保持在多少伏，再算 i_1。
questions.explain: n 点是虚地，电位始终为 0，所以 i_1 = v_1/R_1 只取决于 v_1。各路输入互不影响，这正是反相加法器能做“加权求和”的原因。

hints: 反相端 n 是虚地，每一路输入电流都可以单独算。
虚断：流入 n 的各路电流之和全部流经 R_f。
solution: **1. 负反馈与虚地：** R_f 把输出接回反相端，构成负反馈。同相端接地，v_{+} = 0，由虚短 v_n = 0（虚地）。

en.title: Inverting summing amplifier
statement: In the inverting summer, v_1 = 1 V, v_2 = 2 V, R_1 = 10 kΩ, R_2 = 20 kΩ, R_f = 30 kΩ; the op-amp is ideal.
Find the current i_f in the feedback resistor and the output voltage v_o.

questions.explain: n is a virtual ground: i_1 = 1/10k = 0.1 mA, i_2 = 2/20k = 0.1 mA; by the virtual open, i_f = i_1 + i_2 = 0.2 mA.

questions.ask: If v_2 is changed to 4 V, what happens to the current i_1 in R_1?
choiceExplain: i_f does increase, but which input supplies the extra current? Think about whether the potential of n changes with v_2.
Does a larger v_2 raise the potential of n? Think about how the op-amp adjusts v_o and what potential n stays at, then work out i_1.
questions.explain: Node n is a virtual ground, always at 0 V, so i_1 = v_1/R_1 depends only on v_1. The inputs don't interact — which is exactly why the circuit computes a weighted sum.

hints: The inverting node n is a virtual ground, so each input current can be computed on its own.
Virtual open: the sum of the currents into n all flows through R_f.
solution: **1. Negative feedback and the virtual ground:** R_f connects the output back to the inverting input (negative feedback). The non-inverting input is grounded, v_{+} = 0, so by the virtual short v_n = 0 (virtual ground).
**2. Input currents:** i_1 = v_1/R_1 = 0.1 mA, i_2 = v_2/R_2 = 0.1 mA.
**3. KCL at n (virtual open):** i_f = i_1 + i_2 = **0.2 mA**.
**Check:** the formula v_o = −(R_f/R_1·v_1 + R_f/R_2·v_2) = −(3v_1 + 1.5v_2) = −(3 + 3) = −6 V ✓. Each input is weighted by R_f/R_k, the results are added and inverted.
